  1. 1.dr-order__headThe name over the date, first in the DOM. Title 15/600 in --text-primary; date in the meta step, --text-muted, ellipsised on one line.
  2. 2.dr-wellThe drone doing the job, a 96 × 96 cutout with no ground, closing the row on the right.
  3. 3.dr-statusThe status indicator: a 20px disc on the well's top-right corner with a 2px card-coloured cutout ring.
  4. 4.dr-railThe four-step progress rail. Live orders only.
  5. 5.dr-insetThe From ▸ To strip: --bg-inset, radius 12, padding 16, a 26px neutral direction chip between the stops.
  6. 6.dr-order__feeThe fee as a .dr-number (20/700, tabular) with its word in .dr-sr, and the ETA chip beside it.
  7. 7.dr-btn--primaryThe screen's one green control, on the live card only.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Card (order); Status indicator; Inset strip.

When to use

The order card is the record of one order in a list: order-history and its loading state on the client side, operator-listings on the operator side, where the same card is a job. It is the most measured component in the product. The name leads and the well closes the row, so the reading order and the screen-reader order are the same sequence (WCAG 1.3.2): Package delivery · Today 10:03 · In progress.

The status is never carried by the mark alone. Live green is 1.52:1 on the well and does not clear WCAG 1.4.11 by itself; the live card is also the only one with a rail, an ETA chip and the green CTA, and the mark says In progress outright. Shape and behaviour separate live from done, never colour alone.

The title is the service, not the drone. The fee is a figure with its word in .dr-sr, the CTA is the canonical View details, and the icon actions take their name from aria-label (Delete order). Client side it is an order, operator side a job; the words never cross.

Rule and anti-rule

Do

  • Package delivery Today · 10:03
    Delivery fee₴180 ETA ~6 min
  • Package delivery 28 Jun · 14:20
    Delivery fee₴180

One live order and one delivered, 28 apart on a list that is the screen. The live card spends the screen's one green control; the delivered card answers with a grey icon action.

Don’t

Package delivery 28 Jun · 14:20
Accepted
En route
On-site
Done

A delivered order with a rail of four ticked nodes and a green CTA. Four ticks say nothing and cost 60px, and the green spends a second primary on a list that already has a live order. Drop the rail and use the delivered shape. To make a whole card one tap target instead of carrying a button, use the card that is one link.
